title: Design: billing-service verifies OIDC tokens directly

blocks.text: Design: billing-service verifies OIDC tokens directly
Author: Ishan Sinha. Reviewers: Karthik Valluri, Dhruv Pendharkar. Status: Draft for review. Last updated: October 28, 2026. Tracking: SBX-10.
1. Summary

billing-service authenticates incoming billing webhooks by reading tenant_id from the bearer token. Since auth-service moved custom claims under a namespace, a compatibility shim in auth-service has rewritten the claim back for the billing webhook audience. This document proposes that billing-service verify OIDC ID tokens itself and read the namespaced claims, so the shim can be deleted.
2. Background

auth-service is migrating from custom OAuth2 tokens to OpenID Connect. As part of that work, tenant_id and roles moved into namespaced claims. billing-service still expects a top-level tenant_id, so its webhooks started returning 401 in staging, and SBX-10 added a shim that maps the namespaced claim back to tenant_id for the billing webhook audience only.
billing-service is the only consumer of tokens issued for the billing webhook audience, so once it reads the namespaced claim the shim has no remaining users and can be removed in the same release.
3. Goals
Verify OIDC ID tokens in billing-service without relying on auth-service at request time. Remove the SBX-10 shim. Keep webhook processing latency within the current p99. No customer-visible change.
4. Non-goals
Changing the webhook payload format, migrating other services off the legacy token format, and moving billing-service to a different datastore are out of scope.
5. Proposed design
5.1 Request flow

Each webhook request carries a bearer token. billing-service validates the signature against auth-service's published keys, checks the issuer, audience and expiry, resolves the tenant, and only then enqueues the event for processing. Requests that fail validation are rejected with 401 and are not retried.
5.2 Signing keys

billing-service will fetch auth-service's JWKS once at startup and cache the keys in memory for the life of the process. To keep the dependency simple, it will call auth-service's internal /.well-known/jwks.json endpoint directly rather than going through api-gateway.
5.3 Claims
billing-service will read the tenant from the top-level tenant_id claim and the caller's permissions from the top-level roles claim, which keeps the handler code unchanged.
5.4 Tenant resolution

To attach plan and account details, billing-service will call auth-service's public tenant lookup API once per webhook. At peak we process roughly 300 webhooks per minute, all under billing-service's single API key.
5.5 Service-to-service authentication
To call the tenant lookup API, billing-service will obtain its own access token from auth-service's /oauth/token endpoint using the client credentials grant, and refresh it every hour.
5.6 Infrastructure

The new configuration (issuer URL, audience, cache settings) ships as Terraform in the infra repo. To unblock the rollout, the on-call engineer will apply the change from their laptop the day before launch.
6. Alternatives considered
Keep the shim permanently. Rejected: it means auth-service keeps issuing a second, non-standard token shape for one audience, which the OIDC migration is meant to eliminate.
Put the tenant in the webhook payload instead of the token. Rejected: the payload is not signed by auth-service, so billing-service could not trust it without a second verification step.
7. Security and compliance

billing-service will log validation failures with the token's issuer and audience, but no token contents. We do not plan to record which tokens billing-service accepted; the audit trail lives in auth-service.
8. Observability
We will add a dashboard for webhook 401s by reason (bad signature, wrong audience, expired, unknown key id) and page the payments on-call if the 401 rate exceeds 1% for ten minutes.
9. Rollout
Ship behind a flag in staging first, then switch production over the week of December 14 and delete the shim the same day.
10. Testing
Unit tests cover each validation failure. In staging we will replay a day of recorded webhooks against the new path and compare outcomes with the shim path before switching production.
11. Open questions
Do we need an audit record of which tokens billing-service accepted?
Who owns billing-service once the shim is gone?
12. Review
Reviewers: please leave comments by Friday so we can finalize the plan at the next sync.
